claims: The current boundaries practice guide was updated on 1 June 2026.
Registered title boundaries are normally governed by the general boundaries rule.
Physical features and title-plan edging do not by themselves identify the exact legal boundary.
Boundary ownership and maintenance cannot be inferred solely from the side on which a feature appears.
A boundary agreement recorded in the register does not itself guarantee the exact legal boundary.
A determined boundary shows the exact line of a registered-estate boundary for register purposes.
HM Land Registry records a determined line after the exact line has been identified; it does not resolve the underlying dispute.
Determined-boundary plans must identify start, end and turning points and show sufficient surrounding detail.
The preferred determined-boundary plan scale is no smaller than 1:200.
Measurement-based determined-boundary plans require horizontal measurements accurate to plus or minus 10 millimetres.
A title plan supports the register by graphically representing the general extent of a registered title.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary is shown as determined under section 60.

quality_guards: Do not call an index polygon, title plan or red edging an exact legal boundary.
Do not promote a boundary agreement to a determined boundary.
Require current title identity, register evidence and authoritative polygon or determined-plan bytes for candidate binding.
Keep exact-boundary measurement blocked for all three candidates until those bytes are read back.
